svg.title: Sparse selections become ordered rank-local KV addresses
svg.desc: Top: selection tensors pass through SILKern localization, a masked KV gather and selected attention. Panel a traces rank-zero input [8,5,130,7,-1,262] with two ranks, interleave one and page size 64. Blue, teal and copper identify the survivors 8, 130, 262. Their local positions 4, 65, 131 map through logical pages 0, 1, 2 to physical pages 11, 2, 7, producing 708, 129, 451. Validity bits 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 supply stable destinations 0, 1, 2. Output is [708,129,451,-1,-1,-1], count 3. Panel b draws all 64 slots of physical pages 2, 7, 11, highlighting offsets 1, 3, 4. The page table is nonmonotonic; output retains selection order. Only valid mappings read the table. The example illustrates front compaction for multiple ranks, not the single-rank layout. Python, MLX/Metal and CUDA/Triton share the result with distinct memory ownership.
svg.text: Each cell is one token’s K/V entry.
Physical order differs from selection order.
